answers.reasoning: Perception identifies objects/obstacles; localization estimates robot position and orientation.
Navigation uses understanding to select and execute a collision-free route, rather than merely name objects.
Grasping is manipulation; recognizing human gestures is interaction.
Detecting corrosion/wear is inspection, not changing pose or route.
Vision infers scene properties from images; graphics renders an image from a scene model.
The forward rendering map need not be injective, so inverse graphics is not a uniqueness guarantee.
The analogy maps camera to eye and algorithms to brain, not actuators to sensing.
The actual arrows run lens/sensor to image processing/features and then task outputs.
Angular size constrains a size-to-distance ratio, not either quantity separately.
Raw features require semantic interpretation; the question-mark schematic represents uncertainty, not impossibility.
Early line labeling infers 3D from drawings; pictorial structures use flexible parts.
The visible Marr graphic distinguishes goal from method and does not clearly supply a third distinct level.
Pyramids/scale-space represent multiple resolutions; regularization constrains ill-posed problems, here through smoothness.
The MRF box explicitly associates probabilistic global optimization.
The later column lists SfM reconstruction, computational photography examples and deep learning, not exact invention dates.
Package text is OCR and tolerances are mechanical inspection.
AR tracks references to place virtual objects into live views; stitching merges overlapping views.
Medical imaging analyzes CT/MRI; visual effects includes morphing and stabilization.
Landmarks and motion cues support both map construction and pose estimation.
E(lambda) is a spectral intensity distribution, and wavelength-dependent absorption changes relative components.
The approximate source visible range is 400–700 nanometres, not micrometres or millimetres.
Normalized, truncated axes support the displayed Sun peak near500nm but no absolute power or lamp global-peak inference.
Multiplication by zero reflectance gives zero reflected contribution at that band without requiring zero illumination.
Band responses are8*.25*.5=1 and4*.5*1=2; sum3 relative units.
Rods support sensitive low-light intensity detection; cones daylight color, not lens or mass sensing.
A spectral density needs wavelength-measure units and a radiometric convention; the simplified product alone does not supply those.
L/M/S sensitivity functions overlap rather than forming disjoint single-wavelength detectors.
A channel integrates received spectrum times its own sensitivity, not the highest peak alone.
Linearity gives each doubled input spectrum twice the prior integral under no saturation/adaptation.
A map from many spectral dimensions to three responses can be many-to-one; distinct spectra may share a triplet.
